messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: gpu-inference-prod queue growth detected. queue_size=11.2k (+9.8k in 3m), avg_latency_tokens=420ms, autoscaler_status=FailedToScale. Possible placement/fragmentation symptoms. paging oncall. :rotating_light:

Aisha (oncall): ack-ing. pulling up dashboards. which customers impacted? any obvious errors in allocator or scheduler logs?

Ben (runtime): seeing allocator logs with a lot of `insufficient_contiguous_slices` and `mig_template_mismatch` around the time of the spike. snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T21:03:14Z allocator ERROR: failed allocate slots for request id=abcd-1234 reason=insufficient_contiguous_slices required=3 available_slices=[1,1,2]
2026-03-15T21:03:15Z runtime WARN: binpack-reconcile: no viable placement for pod/model=hf/llama-7b-quantized
```
Not high GPU util overall (~30%), but many small free fragments. smells like MIG sizing mismatch + binpack fragmentation.

Marta (scheduler): confirming from kube-scheduler: a bunch of pending pods with nodeAffinity for `mig=2g.2t` and nodes have different slice topologies. `kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -o wide` shows many waiting for `node-mig-template:2Gx2` which only exists on a subset of nodes. Also we rolled a new model config earlier today that requests 2x-slice.

Priya (mlops): that was my rollout. We pushed variant `v2-big` at 20% traffic to have better latency for a few customers. It requests `gpu.mig=2xA100-7g` via the model-runtime profile. I didn't realize the fleet hadn't been fully reprovisioned with matching MIG templates yet. happy to flip traffic.

Tom R (sre): autoscaler hit `max_nodes=120` per-region quota and refused further scale-up at ~21:05 UTC. metrics: `desired_nodes=145`, `current=120`, `scale_reasons=queue_growth,backlog`. also seeing rate-limit throttle events on API from cloud provider after repeated scale attempts. dashboard: https://rbw/d/dash/gpu-autoscale?panel=queue_growth (internal)

Aisha (oncall): immediate plan: 1) disable v2-big rollout (Priya) -> shift traffic to smaller model. 2) mark some low-priority training jobs for eviction and trigger emergency repack. 3) manual node drains on heavily fragmented nodes to force repack and free contiguous slices. 4) request quota bump from cloud infra (Tom). Also need a short customer note. who can draft?

Priya (mlops): rolling back v2-big now and redirecting traffic to `v1-small` and `v1-medium` fallback. will post when done.

Luis (cs): I'll draft the customer message. short and to the point: "We detected increased response latency and request queuing for inference in region-us-west-2 between 21:00-21:20 UTC. We're mitigating; some requests may have seen delays or 503s. We'll send a full incident update shortly." ok to send as interim?

Aisha (oncall): go ahead with that interim msg, tag affected customers list A+B.

Ben (runtime): starting manual repack sequence. commands:
```
# mark low-priority pods for eviction
kubectl label pod -n infra -l job=background-low-priority eviction=lowprio
# drain targeted nodes (two highly fragmented nodes)
kubectl drain node/node-az3-gpu-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=30
# trigger allocator repack hook
curl -XPOST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://internal-api/repack?mode=aggressive
```
Posting logs as it runs: 
`repack: freed 6 contiguous 2-slice groups, reclaimed 12 slices total`

Marta (scheduler): I'm reprovisioning MIG templates for a subset of nodes to add `2x` slice compatibility but that's disruptive. doing it on a small batch (3 nodes) to validate. also updating scheduler tolerations to allow temporary overcommit to best-effort pods.

Tom R (sre): cloud quota request filed with provider and ops is on a phone call. ETA 45-60m but we can't wait. bumping `max_nodes` to 140 locally (soft cap) to let autoscaler attempt more scale while quota is pending. watch for cost/overprovision.

incident-bot: NOTE: Pager escalation triggered to eng-runtime and scheduler with high urgency.

Priya (mlops): rollback complete at ~21:08 UTC. traffic shifted.

Aisha (oncall): check ingress/router logs to confirm traffic is hitting fallback models and not being rejected.

Ben (runtime): queue size peaked at 11.2k, after repack started queue dropped to 3.4k within 6 minutes, errors 503-> reduced. current queue 1.1k and draining. observed two customers reported timeouts, we have recordings.

Luis (cs): sent interim customer note to affected list. few replies asking for ETA. I told them we're in mitigation and will follow up.

Marta (scheduler): repack + targeted drains freed up contiguous `2-slice` groups on nodes-az2/az3. placement started succeeding for pending pods once freed. scheduler logs: `placement success for 78 pods after repack`.

Aisha (oncall): good. what's root cause summary? and immediate follow-ups?

Ben (runtime): root cause: mixed fleet with mismatched MIG templates + a partial rollout of a model variant that requests larger contiguous MIG slices. combined with aggressive binpack policy caused fragmentation so available slices were scattered; autoscaler couldn't scale up enough due to quota and throttling. result: backlog growth and some 503s.

Marta (scheduler): short-term fixes we did: rollback model, manual repack, targeted node drains, soft-increase autoscaler cap. medium/long term: unify MIG templates across fleet, update deployment gating so model variants requiring larger slices only roll out when fleet compatible, add allocator heuristics to prefer spreading large-slice requests to nodes with contiguous capacity, and autoscaler integration to respect fragmentation metrics not just node count.

Tom R (sre): action items I'm owning: file a request with cloud to permanently raise GPU quota for us-west-2, add alert for `desired_nodes > max_nodes - 5`, and add autoscaler runbook step to check fragmentation before rejecting scale.

Priya (mlops): action items: add canary gating checks that verify node MIG templates match model requirements before rollouts hit >5% traffic. will open PR with gating tests.

Luis (cs): I'll prepare the public incident notification draft for tomorrow with timeline + customer impact.

Aisha (oncall): handoff: I'm handing to Ben and Marta for post-incident cleanup and postmortem. I'll write a short incident timeline and severity. Oncall shift ends in 40m; if anything regress ping me.

Ben (runtime): will keep an eye for 1hr, run follow-up metrics to ensure no slow drift. planning a postmortem doc and will link once created.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: queue_size=1.1k, errors reduced, autoscaler softcap=140, repack successful. incident status: under control. :white_check_mark:
